title: Review an unexpected reading

sources.title: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §3, Health and Medical Care
NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §7, Crew Health Records

summary: A checklist for preparing a reading for crew medical review.
steps: Open the underlying reading and note the value, units, UTC time, instrument, and any quality flag.
Record the activity and symptoms at the time. Compare readings taken under similar conditions when the record allows.
Use the mission-approved measurement and escalation procedure. Share the record with the crew medical officer through the approved channel.

title: Prepare a ground support handoff

sources.title: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §6, Medical Operations
NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §7, Crew Health Records

summary: A handoff template for use with the mission’s medical operations plan.
steps: Use the onboard medical plan and notify the assigned crew medical officer.
Prepare an update with the onset time in UTC, symptoms, activity, readings with units and source, actions already taken, and the latest change.
Transmit the update through the mission-approved private medical channel when available.

title: Document dizziness after a gravity transition

sources.title: NASA OCHMO-TB-019, Orthostatic Intolerance
NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §3, Health and Medical Care

summary: NASA discusses orthostatic intolerance after a return to gravity. Dizziness alone does not establish the cause.
steps: Record when the symptoms began, the gravity transition or activity, and whether symptoms started in an upright position.
Attach any available readings and their source. Use the mission-approved medical evaluation process.

title: Prepare a routine health check

sources.title: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §3.4, In-Mission Preventive Health Care
NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §7, Crew Health Records

summary: NASA includes periodic physical and psychosocial monitoring in preventive crew health care.
steps: Use the mission-defined check schedule and equipment. Record the measurement context and time so subsequent checks can be compared.
Review available trends for general health, fitness, sleep and work/rest schedules, and nutrition as specified in the mission plan.
Save results in the approved health record for review by the flight medicine team.
